title: Hearing Duke at the Lincoln Colonnade in Washington
summary: He heard Ellington's band at dances at the Lincoln Colonnade and got to know the young Ellington men.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, I heard Duke around Washington. You know, I told you I left that school, and I went around Washington, and I heard Duke around there because he played there quite often. So --
MS WILLARD: He had already gone to New York for several years.

Oh, yeah, this is around '29-30 and around in there when I heard a lot of Duke around Washington, because there's a place he used to come and play dances all the time, the Lincoln Colonnade. And you know, it was right next to the Lincoln Theater. This guy Al Leachman owned the Lincoln Theater, and right next door was the Lincoln Colonnade, and most all the big bands used to come there and play dances.
And you could really hear a band at a dance much better than you could at a concert because you could hang right around the band, right around the stand and really get an earful, you know.
And I got to the point where I knew a lot of guys because I knew where they unloaded their instruments to come

from the back of the stage, you know, little street in the back. So I got to know a lot of guys, and they were young guys with Duke back then. Johnny and them were very young, you know. This was '29-30, back at that time.

And I was doing a little playing around Washington, and so the guy I played for, Booker Coleman, and also Tommy Miles. All those guys knew, and they were older than I, and lot of the guys with Duke and them knew them, because they'd -- they'd played around with them before, you know.
So I got good exposure, you know, way back, you know, but --
